records.claim: CFCFRMS saved more than Rs 11,158 crore across more than 32.80 lakh complaints by 30 June 2026; 1930 helpline operational.
records.evidence_summary: The MHA/PIB release states the CFCFRMS figures through 30 June 2026 and identifies 1930 as the toll-free assistance number.

records.claim: UPI PIN must not be shared; only sending money requires UPI PIN.
records.evidence_summary: NPCI's safety-check screen states that UPI PIN should be entered only on the UPI PIN page, only sending money requires UPI PIN, and OTP should not be shared.

records.claim: 'Scan a QR code to receive money' is fraudulent when it is coupled with UPI PIN entry; QR+PIN is a payment act, not a receipt act.
records.evidence_summary: NPCI warns that unknown links/QR codes promising rewards may ask for UPI PIN and says scanning a QR plus entering UPI PIN is for making payments, not receiving them. The same snapshot also warns about remote-access/screen-sharing apps during financial transactions.

records.claim: Executive/regulator impersonation ('boss scam') can culminate in urgent payment instructions over messaging channels.
records.evidence_summary: The release describes regulator impersonation, urgent compliance pretexts, WhatsApp takeover and immediate transfer instructions to finance staff.

records.claim: Social-media stock scams may impersonate public figures/celebrities and use fake testimonials and unreasonable-return promises.
records.evidence_summary: SEBI's body text supports celebrity/public-figure impersonation and fake-profit social-media funnels, but the archived body does not contain a deepfake-specific statement.

records.claim: Screen-recording/screen-sharing applications are a banking security threat.
records.evidence_summary: The current HDFC page tells users to close screen-recording/screen-sharing apps and explicitly names AnyDesk, TeamViewer and AirDroid.

records.claim: Replacement snapshot for the dead HDFC fraud page.
unsupported_elements: the manifest does not list claim_under_test/blocks_rules for SRC-008
this snapshot does not by itself verify all five rules said to depend on the dead page
records.evidence_summary: Useful official HDFC replacement material was captured, but it cannot be treated as a full substitute for the old SIM-swap/beware-of-fraud citation without per-rule reconciliation.

records.issuer: CyberDost / I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs
records.claim: Unknown callers can misuse call-forwarding codes; users should not dial unverified telecom codes.
supported_elements: warning not to dial unverified codes
unsupported_elements: courier/delivery pretext is not present in the captured CyberDost post
records.evidence_summary: The official CyberDost channel substantiates the call-forwarding/code-abuse mechanism, but not the specific delivery-agent pretext in TL-TEL-001.

records.issuer: CyberDost / I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs
records.claim: Android malware can abuse Accessibility permissions to gain unauthorized control, with fake apps/APKs/links as delivery.
records.evidence_summary: The official CyberDost post says Android God Mode misuses Accessibility permissions, impersonates trusted services, and is delivered via links/APKs/fake apps.

records.issuer: CyberDost / I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs
records.claim: Trust Wallet users can be moved from P2P contact to WhatsApp/Telegram, sent to fake verification sites, asked to connect the wallet, and drained after permissions are approved.
records.evidence_summary: The official CyberDost post closely matches the blocked Trust Wallet rule concept, including the off-platform handoff, fake verification website, wallet connection and permission-based transfer.

records.claim: Apps delivered through messages/links outside trusted sources are risky malware-delivery vectors.
supported_elements: do not install apps from chat/social links
records.evidence_summary: CERT-In strongly supports the generic non-store/untrusted-link app-install rule, but not the iOS configuration-profile clause in TL-MAL-001.

records.issuer: PIB / Ministry of Home Affairs / I4C
records.claim: Task-based part-time job scam progression from ad to WhatsApp/Telegram tasks, initial commission, larger investment and frozen deposits.
records.evidence_summary: The MHA/PIB release verifies the trust-building and deposit-freeze portion of the blocked TL-JOB-003 sequence.

records.issuer: NCTAU / I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs
records.claim: Fake part-time task platforms can deny withdrawals and demand additional payments such as taxes, processing charges, commissions or membership upgrades.
records.evidence_summary: This I4C advisory supplies the blocked-withdrawal and further-payment portion of TL-JOB-003.
